skill.name: fetching-library-docs
skill.description: Fetches current library documentation through Context7 MCP, then filters the results into concise code examples, API signatures, and key notes.
skill.summary: Fetch concise, current library API documentation with Context7 MCP filtering.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: The skill has a legitimate purpose: fetching and filtering library documentation from Context7. Most static findings are false positives from markdown examples, awk output, and expected shell pipeline use, but the bundled generic MCP client exposes direct shell execution through --stdio, and the helper scripts use npx package execution plus predictable /tmp PID files.

remediation.issue: Generic MCP client allows arbitrary stdio commands through shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Remove direct --stdio exposure from the marketplace skill, or replace shell=True with an allowlisted argv array for the Context7 command only.

remediation.issue: Scripts execute @upstash/context7-mcp through npx -y at runtime.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the package version, document the network execution requirement, and prefer a locked dependency installation path over implicit runtime download.

remediation.issue: Server control scripts trust a predictable PID file in /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Store PID files in a user-owned runtime directory with safe permissions, validate PID ownership before killing, and avoid broad pkill patterns.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled Stdio Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The generic MCP client accepts a --stdio command and starts it with subprocess.Popen using shell=True. Direct use of scripts/mcp-client.py can execute arbitrary shell commands, even though the main skill workflow uses a fixed Context7 command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command string comes from the --stdio argument and is passed to Popen with shell=True. This is a direct local command execution path when the helper is used outside the fixed wrapper scripts.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Package Execution with npx
semantic_findings.description: The skill starts Context7 by running npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp. This downloads or executes a package during skill use, which creates supply-chain and network execution risk if the package source is compromised.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scripts explicitly use npx -y to execute the Context7 MCP package. This appears intentional, but it is still a real external package execution risk.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable PID File Can Target Local Processes
semantic_findings.description: The start and stop scripts store a process id in /tmp/context7-mcp-${PORT}.pid and later pass that value to kill. A stale or tampered PID file could cause the stop script to terminate an unrelated local process.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The PID file path is predictable and located in /tmp, and stop-server.sh trusts its contents. The impact is local process termination rather than data theft.

content.value_statement: Developers often need current API examples without loading full documentation into the model context. This skill fetches Context7 library docs and returns focused examples, signatures, and notes.
actual_capabilities: Resolves common library names to Context7-compatible library identifiers.
Fetches documentation for published libraries through the Context7 MCP server.
Filters raw documentation into code examples, API signatures, and important notes.
Supports code-focused and conceptual documentation modes.
Supports pagination for broader documentation exploration.
Provides shell scripts for starting, stopping, and verifying the Context7 helper workflow.
limitations: Requires network access and the Context7 MCP package to be available.
Only covers libraries available through Context7 documentation sources.
Does not inspect local repository internals or private source code.
Filtered output may omit surrounding context from the full documentation page.

use_cases.title: Look up framework APIs
use_cases.description: Fetch focused examples for React hooks, Next.js routing, Prisma queries, or similar framework features.

use_cases.title: Learn an unfamiliar library
use_cases.description: Start with conceptual docs, then request code examples for the same package or feature.

use_cases.title: Reduce documentation context size
use_cases.description: Use shell filtering to keep large documentation responses out of the model context.
use_cases.target_user: Claude Code and Codex power users

prompt_templates.title: Get a simple API example
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one library feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch the current documentation for React useState and show the most relevant examples.

prompt_templates.title: Compare usage patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for several examples from one package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the library docs skill to find Next.js routing examples, then summarize the main patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Learn a package workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured exploration of a new library.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch Prisma getting started information first, then fetch query examples and explain the workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Research multiple pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch React hooks documentation across the first two pages, then identify advanced patterns and important caveats.

output_examples.output: A concise response with selected useState examples, matching API signatures, and key notes from current Context7 documentation.
A short conceptual overview with a few routing examples and links between the relevant routing concepts.

output_examples.input: Find Prisma query syntax and important warnings.
output_examples.output: A focused summary of query methods, representative examples, and extracted notes about safe or recommended usage.

best_practices: Use a specific library name and topic to get focused results.
Use code mode for API examples and info mode for concepts.
Use a known Context7 library ID when you already have one.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to inspect local repository files.
Do not request private or unpublished package documentation through Context7.
Do not bypass the filtered fetch script unless you need raw MCP debugging.

faq.question: Does this skill work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What documentation source does it use?
faq.answer: It uses the Context7 MCP server to resolve library IDs and fetch documentation.

faq.question: Can it read my local project files?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for published library documentation, not local repository analysis.

faq.question: Why does it filter the documentation?
faq.answer: Filtering returns the most useful examples and notes while reducing model context usage.

faq.question: Can I ask for conceptual explanations?
faq.answer: Yes. Use info mode when you want concepts, architecture, or narrative guidance.

faq.question: What are the main security considerations?
faq.answer: It uses network access, runtime package execution, shell scripts, and a generic MCP helper that should be restricted before publication.
